clue.text: Awfully hard potato father failing to finish immediately

indicators.note: done awfully, the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the word father stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut short

explanation.surface: A dreadful dad and a hard potato, with a hint of failing at the last.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly and without hesitation, as if on the signal of a hat being dropped.

clue.text: No heading for legal rubbish

indicators.note: the word for legal loses its leading letter, its head

parts.note: lawful is a synonym of legal

explanation.surface: A complaint that legal writing lacks a heading, which makes it rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: As an informal adjective it means very bad, the sense of rubbish as poor quality.

clue.text: Tense Yankee drinking pub beer in Sydney?

indicators.note: the outer pair of letters takes in, swallows, the pub

parts.note: Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A nervous American downing a pint in an Australian bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is Australian slang, hence Sydney.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang this is a can of beer, so a Sydneysider's drink.

clue.text: Returning east, Greek character hollow and empty

indicators.note: in a down clue the run of pieces comes back, read from bottom to top

parts.note: tau is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
a cave is a hollow in rock

explanation.surface: A traveller coming back east finds a Greek figure hollow and empty.
explanation.walkthrough: Hollow looks like an adjective for the Greek character but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: To evacuate a building is to clear it, a verb synonym of empty.

clue.text: Assess speed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to judge the value of
second meaning: a noun, the pace at which something moves

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for valuing or judging and a noun for pace, as in a rate of knots.

clue.text: Scarred grassland ridiculed by Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two pieces trade initial consonants

parts.note: mocked is a synonym of ridiculed, said aloud with a hard final t sound
a park is an area of grassland

explanation.surface: A field mocked by a famously muddled clergyman ends up scarred.
explanation.walkthrough: Mocked park, with its first sounds swapped, says pocked mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin left pitted by spots or disease such as smallpox is described as scarred this way.

clue.text: Rich and powerful person from Florida upset Prudence

parts.note: FA is a postal-style abbreviation used for Florida

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word for prudence on its head, reading upwards

parts.note: tact is diplomacy or prudence

explanation.surface: A tycoon from Florida offends a woman called Prudence.
explanation.walkthrough: Prudence is capitalised to look like a woman's name; it is the quality of discretion.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a wealthy, influential figure, often a highly paid executive.

clue.text: Locally hot before a boxing match

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
taken as written
a bout is a boxing contest

explanation.surface: A local fight announced on a hot day.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in this vicinity, nearby, which is to say in the local area.

clue.text: Last touch of paint on miniature is pretty

indicators.note: the final letter, the closing touch, of paint is taken

parts.note: only its last letter is used
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: An artist's final brushstroke on a tiny portrait makes it pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means excessively quaint or cutesy, a sugary kind of prettiness.

clue.text: Weird admirer thanks Rod endlessly

parts.note: a fan is an admirer
ta is British informal for thank you

indicators.note: the word for rod loses its final letter, so it has no end

parts.note: a stick is a rod

explanation.surface: A strange fan keeps thanking someone named Rod over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod looks like a name at the start of the sentence; it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean bizarre or fanciful, far removed from reality, the older sense of strange.

clue.text: Undergrad's heart checked by you once in Trinity?

indicators.note: the central letter is held in check, enclosed, by the old pronoun

parts.note: thee is an archaic form of you

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the word undergrad, whose central letter alone is used

explanation.surface: A student at Trinity College being reined in by an old-fashioned tutor.
explanation.walkthrough: Trinity suggests the Cambridge college; the question mark says it is a definition by example of a group of that many.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinity is a set of persons or things numbering this, as in the Holy Trinity.

clue.text: Floor plan

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to knock someone down flat
second meaning: a noun, an arrangement or design

explanation.walkthrough: Floor plan reads as one architectural term but splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means to knock someone flat, and as a noun it is the arrangement of a page or room.

clue.text: African antelope? The setter's friend with answer

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so the setter's or setter is becomes I'm
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: The setter asks whether an African antelope is a friend with the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is a graceful antelope of southern and eastern African grasslands, a specific species.

clue.text: Pleasant situation, or a thorny one?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an easy, comfortable state of affairs
second meaning, playful: literally a flower bed full of prickly plants

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is usually said in the negative, life is no such thing; the second reading takes it literally as a prickly garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an easy, comfortable life, while a literal garden plot of these flowers bristles with thorns.

clue.text: Prophet close to Chaucer south of Canterbury?

indicators.note: in a down clue the last letter sits below the diocese

parts.note: Canterbury is an archbishop's see, a diocese

indicators.note: the close, the end, of Chaucer gives its final letter

parts.note: only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A soothsayer near Chaucer, author of The Canterbury Tales, on the road south.
explanation.walkthrough: Canterbury's question mark flags it as an example of a see, the seat of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer is one who sees the future, a synonym for a prophet or visionary.

clue.text: Steady tweeter has gone mad

indicators.note: gone mad means the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone posting on social media has lost their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Has does double duty in the surface but its letters belong in the fodder; gone mad is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is an old-fashioned word for a regular boyfriend or girlfriend, a beloved partner.

clue.text: Block small dog

parts.note: lab is short for Labrador, a dog breed

explanation.surface: An order to stop a little dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slab is a thick flat block of stone, wood or similar material.

clue.text: Tossing a coin, game's narcissist

indicators.note: tossing throws the letters about, like a coin in the air

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the word game, with the apostrophe s serving as is linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A coin flipped to start a match, with a self-absorbed player.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossing a coin sounds like the start of a match; tossing is the signal, a coin and game the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcissist is a person obsessed with self-importance, which matches someone wholly self-centred.

clue.text: Conservative fine with European fuel

parts.note: OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A Tory politician satisfied with European energy supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is a solid fuel made by heating coal, used in furnaces and smelting.

clue.text: Maybe son's resistance over Glee

indicators.note: in a down clue the resistance symbol is placed over, above, the joy

parts.note: elation is great joy or glee

explanation.surface: A son, perhaps, shows resistance to joining the choir in a Glee club.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the physics symbol for resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is one example of a kinsman, a family member connected by blood.

clue.text: Very small part in rejected demo tape

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the hidden letters read backwards
the letters sit inside the run of words demo tape

parts.note: the letters are found spanning these two words

explanation.surface: A band's tiny bit on a demo tape that the record label turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest unit of a chemical element, a tiny particle.

clue.text: Romantic note from landlady with nothing on?

indicators.note: in an across clue on means put before, so zero comes first

parts.note: love is a score of zero in tennis
a letter is one who lets property, as a landlady does

explanation.surface: A saucy message from a landlady wearing nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Landlady is a playful example: one who lets rooms is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A love letter is a written message expressing affection for a sweetheart.

clue.text: Play at home and admit defeat

parts.note: give is slack or play, as in a rope
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Playing a home match and conceding the loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in is to surrender or yield, conceding that one has lost.

clue.text: Advanced through tracks where birds are gathered

parts.note: via means by way of, through
RY is short for railway, a set of tracks

explanation.surface: Going forward along the paths where flocks of birds have assembled.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is a large enclosure in which birds are kept together.

clue.text: Test series past 500 runs

indicators.note: the Test series comes after, past, the Roman numeral

parts.note: the Ashes is the cricket Test series between England and Australia

explanation.surface: A cricket Test series in which a batsman passes 500 runs.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals. The cricket picture makes runs look like scoring; it is a verb meaning sprints.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash is to run quickly, so this form is a synonym of runs, as in sprints.

clue.text: Arthur still collecting wood

indicators.note: the two words collect, hold, the answer across their join

parts.note: the letters are hidden spanning these words

explanation.surface: Arthur is still out gathering firewood.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurst is an old word for a wooded hill or grove, familiar from English place names.

clue.text: I must leave older Spanish gentleman

indicators.note: the letter I has to go, departing from the word for older

parts.note: senior means older
the letter I, taken as written from the clue

explanation.surface: A speaker announces they must depart before an older Spanish man arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Señor is the Spanish title and form of address for a man, equal to sir or mister.

clue.text: Boundless confidence for exam

indicators.note: with no bounds the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: morale is a group's confidence or spirit

explanation.surface: Feeling limitless self-belief going into a test.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in a language test.

clue.text: Fruit drops rapidly, 50 per cent off

indicators.note: half of the word is removed, the second four of its eight letters

parts.note: plummets means falls fast

explanation.surface: Fruit prices crash with a half-price sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum is a soft stone fruit with purple or yellow skin.

clue.text: Amplify Charles and Johnnie perhaps for the audience

indicators.note: for listeners, the word sounds like the pair of surnames

parts.note: Ray Charles and Johnnie Ray are both singers named Ray

explanation.surface: Turn up the volume on two famous singers for the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray Charles and Johnnie Ray were American singers sharing the name Ray, one as a first name, one as a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise is to increase or heighten, as raising volume amplifies a sound.

clue.text: Tommy showing? Stick at it!

parts.note: Tommy Atkins is slang for a British private soldier
a film that is on is showing

explanation.surface: Is the film about a British army private on, and will it keep going?
explanation.walkthrough: A Tommy is a British infantryman, from Tommy Atkins.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going through difficulty is to persevere, as the exhortation urges.

clue.text: Legendary swimmer left windy shore with Scotsmen around noon

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the letter for noon
windy suggests the letters blown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mythical creature leaves a blustery beach with Scots at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: N is noon as on a clock face; the Highland setting is apt for the famous creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the mythical beast said to swim in a deep Scottish lake near Inverness.
